observation_summary: The MathUtils.equals method incorrectly returns true when comparing two NaN values, which violates the IEEE 754 standard where NaN is not equal to itself.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a failure to correctly implement the equality contract for NaN values. This is a logic error in the conditional check used to determine equality. Since the fix involves correcting the predicate logic (the condition that determines if two doubles are equal), it falls under the Checking category.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'In MathUtils, some equals methods will return true if both argument are NaN. Unless I'm mistaken, this contradicts the IEEE standard.'

The failing test case is org.apache.commons.math.util.MathUtilsTest::testArrayEquals, which asserts that two arrays containing NaN should NOT be equal (assertFalse(MathUtils.equals(new double[] { Double.NaN }, new double[] { Double.NaN })));

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the equality check is a method, the core issue is the logic of the conditional check (the guard) for NaN, which is more specifically a Checking defect.
